Throughout human history, species have become extinct, and the degradation of ecosystems is likely to accelerate further in the com- ing years (Johnson et al. 2017). Earth S biodiversity is facing an unprecedented crisis, with ecosystems dete- riorating alarmingly due to several sorts of pollution, land-use change (including biodiversity loss, habitat destruction, and fragmentation), climate change, and the introduction of non-indigenous species (NIS) (Gaston et al. 2023). The ocean is no exception, with modified marine ecosystems experiencing accelerat- ing species loss with largely unknown consequences (Boris Worm et al. 2006; Nagelkerken and Connell 2022). In this context, global initiatives, such as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Frame- work (GBF), have been established to recognise the urgency of these circumstances.

This framework has 23 action-oriented global targets for urgent action to reverse biodiversity decline over the decade until 2030. nodes.paragraph: As the global com- munity faces escalating challenges such as climate change, resource depletion, and bio- diversity loss, the need for practical, scalable, and equitable environmental protection strategies has become critical. International efforts, such as the World Bank S Global Program on Sustainability (GPS), underscore the importance of integrating environmen- tal considerations into public and private sector decision-making (GPS, 2019). Socioeconomic inequalities further amplify these challenges, hindering coop- eration in sustainability efforts and contributing to biodiversity loss (Baland et al., 2018; Mikkelson et al., 2007). A growing body of research highlights the crucial role of socioeconomic factors such as income, education, and employment stability in shaping environmental attitudes and behaviors, with distinct patterns emerging between higher and lower socioeconomic groups. Higher socioeconomic groups, characterized by greater financial stability and envi- ronmental awareness, are more likely to engage in pro-environmental behaviors, including energy-saving measures and sustainable consumption practices (Du et al., 2024; Ivkovi & Mandi , 2024; Meyer, 2016).
